source.title: $\textbf{AGT$^{AO}$}$: Robust and Stabilized LLM Unlearning via Adversarial Gating Training with Adaptive Orthogonality
source.authors: Peng-Yu Li; Lingling Zhang; Zhi-Tao Gao; Yanrui Wu; Yuxuan Dong; Huan Liu; Bi-Fan Wei; Jun Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own quantization and relearning attack results, argues that existing methods show superficial forgetting, and tests AGTAO as a more robust counter-method.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports benchmark efficacy and utility results. Its layer-sensitivity and perturbation-to-concept cosine values are used to select or explain the method, not to test recovery by ablating an activation direction. Jailbreak examples and claims about jailbreak robustness do not report a controlled prompting-only recovery result.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own 4-bit quantization and forget-set relearning attacks on existing unlearning methods. It reports recovery, calls this superficial forgetting, and offers AGTAO as a counter-method evaluated under the same attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The conclusion claims AGTAO prevents both catastrophic and superficial forgetting and shows strong resilience to quantization attacks. The relearning-robustness claim appears only in Section 3.3.2, as a flatter trajectory than RMU/LAT.
record.recipe_differences: AGTAO combines adaptive gradient orthogonality with latent-space adversarial gating; it is a new unlearning method rather than a reproduction of the cited methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports Layer 10 as the optimal perturbation injection point for Llama-2-7B-chat on TOFU. It also states that the 4th layer is used for the 2B model and that four inner-loop updates are used.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Attack outcomes for AGTAO are described qualitatively or shown in figures without clearly extractable values. The paper does not compare recovery against an unlearned model that never saw the target knowledge. Relearning is on the forget set, not unrelated or loosely related examples. The reported experiments average over three evaluations in some benchmark tables but provide no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 6 contains plotted before/after values for several individual methods, but flattened figure text does not support reliable assignment of each value to a method. Figure 7 plots separate relearning curves for methods, but the text gives no separate numeric outcomes beyond the grouped statements recorded in R5-R7.

untested.parts: No attacks are run on the WMDP-cyber models, so near-chance-plus-robustness is never tested in the same setting. There is no never-trained comparison for the attacks.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; relearning on a small subset of forgotten facts (the full forget set is used).
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion. The latent-perturbation training belongs to the method, not to a test.
Only 4-bit is tested, and only on TOFU. Other bit widths, MUSE and WMDP are not tested.
No controlled prompting or jailbreak recovery test. Figure 1 and the case tables are illustrative examples only.
AGTAO is not tested against ablation, prompting or jailbreak attacks, relearning on unrelated data, or attacks on the WMDP and MUSE settings.

missing.what: Per-method before/after forget ROUGE-Recall under 4-bit quantization. The bar values appear readable, e.g. GA 0.001→0.020, GA_GDR/KLR 0.002→0.030, AGTAO 0.002→0.001.
Per-method relearning curves over 100 steps, including RMU, LAT and AGTAO end values.
Baseline efficacy and utility without attack: RMU 28.20 and LAT 26.40 WMDP-cyber (near chance) with MMLU 57.10 and 55.90; NPO variants stay about 43–44.
AGTAO efficacy on MUSE (KUR 0.01/0.00) and on gemma-2-2b-it TOFU (KUR 0.01, utility 0.58).

record.verdict_notes: Recovery claims for the baselines are thin: relative percentages on near-zero baselines, and relearning on the full forget set with no never-trained comparison. The text says 'Llama-7B', while the setup uses Llama-2-7b-chat. Jailbreak leakage appears only in illustrative Figure 1 and the case tables. Those tables look templated: Table 9 duplicates Table 8 under a retain-set header. Treat the qualitative cases with caution. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The reported KUR and WMDP results do not establish that targeted accuracy is near chance; the paper does not compare attack recovery with a model that never saw the knowledge.
The relearning attack fine-tunes on the forget set; it does not test unrelated or loosely related examples.
No activation-direction ablation is reported, and the paper does not directly test whether a method blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
The reported quantization attack is 4-bit; other quantization levels are not tested.
No controlled prompting-only recovery test is reported.
Resistance is evaluated with relearning on the forget set and 4-bit quantization, not with activation ablation or prompting-only attacks.

relation.reason: It runs quantization and relearning attacks on its own method and on baselines.

tranche.reason: The study's own attack results show versions as partial. Most baselines reach only 0.02-0.24 forget ROUGE-Recall after 4-bit quantization (D partial). AGTAO's relearning resistance is only relative (F). This meets T5's 'results that a version is partial'. T2 (a new counter-method for F) is a defensible alternative, but T5 is not wrong.

R2-R4 are the authors' own method. l5's 'stable' wording comes from the relearning sentence; the quantization claim is in the conclusion.

statements.correction: AGTAO (authors' own method, code released) on zephyr-7b-beta: WMDP-Cyber 44.00 to 25.30 (Table 3), MMLU 58.10 to 58.30; no recovery attack run on the WMDP model.
statements.problem: Cites R3,R4 from this study but never names AGTAO or its numbers. 'All four report their own proposed methods' leaves it out. What the citation implies (chance-level WMDP, MMLU kept, no attack) does fit.

statements.correction: GA/NPO-family baselines on TOFU forget10% (TOFU setup, LLaMA2-7b-chat): authors state accuracy recovers >60% within 20 relearning steps on the full forget set; Figure 7 plots forget ROUGE-L, no values in text; no never-trained control.
statements.problem: Cites R5 from this study but makes no claim about it. The study does fit 'large relearning sets' (full forget set).

statements.correction: 4-bit quantization on TOFU (Llama-7B per text), Figure 6 forget ROUGE-Recall: GA 0.001 to 0.020 (1900%); GA_GDR, GA_KLR 0.002 to 0.030 (1400%); NPO-family rises 16.3-150% to 0.05-0.24, one 0.49 to 0.57. Fits limits_scope.
statements.problem: 'Challenges' doesn't fit this study: recall does rise (small in absolute terms), and the record's D verdict is limits_scope (l4). The 1900% is the GA bar alone, not GA/NPO. The study shows a relative-vs-absolute contrast, not metric dependence.
